items.title: Italy recovers 19 bodies from migrant boat near Lampedusa

featured_image.name: 19 Migrants Found Dead by Italian Coastguard off Lampedusa

items.description: Italy's coast guard recovered the bodies of 19 migrants and rescued 58 survivors from a dinghy that broke down while attempting to cross the central Mediterranean from Libya, officials said on Wednesday. The vessel was intercepted on Tuesday night roughly 80 nautical miles south of the island of Lampedusa amid rough weather conditions.[1][2][3]

items.description: Analysts estimate the US is burning through high-end weapons in Iran at a rate that could take years to replenish, risking the West's military readiness for other potential conflicts.

items.title: UK to host 35-nation summit on reopening Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Labour Suspends MP Karl Turner as Starmer Faces Internal ...

items.description: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced on Wednesday that the UK will host a virtual summit of approximately 35 countries on Thursday to discuss diplomatic and military steps to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway effectively shut down by the ongoing conflict between the US and Israel against Iran.

items.title: Trump demands Iran reopen Strait of Hormuz, threatens to 'obliterate' infrastructure

featured_image.name: Trump urges countries seeking oil to go to Strait of Hormuz ...

items.description: As the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran enters its second month, Tehran has moved to formalize its control over the Strait of Hormuz, demanding international recognition of its sovereignty over the critical waterway as a condition for ending the conflict — a stance that has drawn sharp rebukes from Washington and rattled global energy markets.

items.title: Seizing Iran's uranium by force would risk casualties, experts warn

featured_image.name: Securing Iran's highly-enriched uranium stockpiles could prove risky,  experts say | Euronews

items.description:
Should the United States attempt to seize Iran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium by military force, the operation would require as many as 1,000 specially trained troops, carry radiation and chemical hazards, and likely result in casualties, according to experts and former government officials.[1]

The warning, detailed in an Associated Press report from Vienna, underscores the tension between President Donald Trump's stated goal that Iran will "never have a nuclear weapon" and the practical difficulties of achieving it on the ground.[1]

items.title: Macron reaffirms France won't join US-Israel war on Iran

featured_image.name: Macron calls for ceasefire in Mideast during visit to Japan

items.description:
Speaking at a joint press conference with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Tokyo on Wednesday, French President Emmanuel Macron firmly restated that France has no role in the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran and was never asked to participate.

"It is absolutely true that France, which was not consulted and is not part of the military offensive launched by the United States and Israel, is not taking part," Macron told reporters, according to French news channel BFMTV.[1]

items.title: Albanese will today try to defend his prime-time message
items.description: With no realistic end in sight and a whole lot of economic pain to come, the PM's decision to make a direct plea to the nation was not one taken lightly.

items.title: Israel kills Hezbollah's Southern Front commander in Beirut naval strike

featured_image.name: Israeli Strike in Beirut Kills Hezbollah Commander for Iraq

items.description: Israeli naval forces killed Hajj Yusuf Ismail Hashem, the commander of Hezbollah's Southern Front, in a strike on Beirut early Wednesday, the Israel Defense Forces announced. The attack on the Jnah district of the Lebanese capital was one of two Israeli strikes in the Beirut area overnight that killed at least seven people and wounded more than two dozen others, according to Lebanon's health ministry.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Trump to address nation on Iran as war enters day 33

featured_image.name: Trump to address nation with 'important update' on Iran

items.description:
The U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its 33rd day on Wednesday, with Israel reporting it has carried out more than 800 combat sorties using approximately 16,000 munitions since Operation Roaring Lion began on February 28, while Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced the 89th wave of its "True Promise-4" retaliatory campaign, deploying over 100 heavy missiles, combat drones, and around 200 rocket projectiles at U.S. and Israeli positions across the region.[1][2][3][4][5][6]

President Donald Trump is set to deliver a national address at 9 p.m. ET Wednesday to provide what the White House called "an important update" on Iran, after saying Tuesday that U.S. forces would be "leaving soon" and predicting the conflict could end within two to three weeks.[7][8][9]

items.title: Trump ties ceasefire talks to reopening Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: We will consider when Hormuz is open': Trump says Iran seeking ceasefire

items.description: Iran has made international recognition of its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz a central condition for any ceasefire in the ongoing war with the United States and Israel, deepening a crisis that has upended global energy markets and sent oil prices soaring past $100 a barrel.

items.title: Shell in advanced talks to develop major gas fields in Venezuela

featured_image.name: Shell Moves Ahead With Venezuela Gas Project After U.S. ... - Oil Price

items.description:
Shell is in advanced negotiations with Venezuela's government to develop four large offshore natural gas areas near Trinidad and Tobago, in what would represent a major expansion of the energy giant's footprint in the country, Reuters reported on Tuesday.[1]

The talks center on two of South America's largest offshore gas deposits, with combined reserves of roughly 20 trillion cubic feet. Shell is seeking access to three fields that form part of the 12-tcf Mariscal Sucre project off Venezuela's east coast — including the flagship 4.2-tcf Dragon field — as well as the 7.3-tcf Loran offshore field, which straddles the maritime border with Trinidad, according to two people familiar with the discussions.[2][1]
